knowledge:
- key_parameters: method in normalize()=Supports "tic" (total-ion-current, standard for MSI), "rms" (root-mean-square, best for differing spectrum lengths), or "reference" (normalizes to a constant reference peak) ;; method in smooth()=Supports "gaussian", "bilateral", "adaptive" (adaptive bilateral), "diff" (nonlinear diffusion), "guide" (guided filtering), "pag" (peak-aware guided), "sgolay" (Savitzky-Golay), or "ma" (moving average) ;; method in reduceBaseline()=Supports "locmin" (local minima interpolation), "hull" (convex hull), "snip" (sensitive nonlinear iterative peak clipping), or "median" (running medians) ;; method in recalibrate()=Supports "locmax" (local regression), "dtw" (dynamic time warping), or "cow" (correlation optimized warping) ;; method in peakPick()=Supports "diff" (derivative-based noise estimation), "sd" or "mad" (wavelet-based noise estimation), "quantile" (rolling quantile), "filter" (dynamic peak filtering), or "cwt" (continuous wavelet transform) ;; BPPARAM=Specifies the parallel backend (e.g., SerialParam(), MulticoreParam(), SnowParam()) for parallel processing ;; sampleSize in peakProcess()=Specifies the fraction of spectra (e.g., 0.3) used to generate reference peaks before full-dataset summarization ;; r, k, s in spatialShrunkenCentroids()=r is the spatial smoothing neighborhood radius, k is the initial number of clusters, and s is the sparsity threshold (higher s retains fewer features)
- alternatives: MulticoreParam() vs SnowParam()=MulticoreParam() uses forking and is faster but only works on macOS/Linux, whereas SnowParam() uses socket connections and works on Windows but has higher overhead ;; PLS() vs OPLS()=Both perform supervised classification, but O-PLS (orthogonal PLS) can produce more easily interpretable regression coefficients ;; meansTest() on raw data vs meansTest() on spatialDGMM()=Segment-based testing using spatial-DGMM captures within-sample heterogeneity and is more sensitive than sample-mean-based testing
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) datasets (e.g., MALDI, DESI) to perform spatial exploratory analysis, image segmentation, pixel-level classification, or statistical class comparisons across multiple experimental runs or conditions.
- pitfalls: Out-of-memory crashes=Raw spectra are kept out-of-memory by default; coercing large datasets to dense in-memory matrices (e.g., using as.matrix() on spectra()) can easily exhaust system memory ;; Slow image plotting=Plotting ion images from out-of-memory datasets is slow because data is stored spectrum-by-spectrum; coerce to an in-memory matrix first if rapid visualization is required ;; Cross-validation bias=When cross-validating, ensure all spectra from the same experimental run belong to the same fold (using folds=run(x)) to prevent run-effect bias ;; Combining datasets=cbind() requires identical m/z values across datasets; preprocessing (e.g., peak alignment or binning) is necessary before combining ;; ROI selection=Always specify a subset (e.g., a single run) in selectROI(), otherwise selection across multiple runs may yield unexpected results

workflows.name: msi_preprocessing_and_peak_extraction
workflows.intent: Import raw MSI data, apply sequential preprocessing steps, perform peak picking and alignment, and export the processed dataset.
input: processed.imzML (raw processed MSI data with differing m/z values)
workflows.stages:
1. Read raw MSI data using readMSIData()
2. Queue preprocessing steps: normalize(), smooth(), reduceBaseline(), and peakPick()
3. Preview queued processing using plot()
4. Apply processing and align peaks across spectra using peakAlign()
5. Filter peaks by frequency using subsetFeatures()
6. Export the processed dataset to imzML using writeMSIData()
workflows.code:
path_continuous <- CardinalIO::exampleImzMLFile("continuous")
mse_tiny <- readMSIData(path_continuous)
path_processed <- CardinalIO::exampleImzMLFile("processed")
msa_tiny <- readMSIData(path_processed)
mse_queue <- msa |>
	normalize() |>
	smooth() |>
	reduceBaseline() |>
	peakPick(SNR=6)
plot(mse_queue, coord=list(x=16, y=16), linewidth=2)
mse_proc <- peakAlign(mse_queue)
mse_proc <- subsetFeatures(mse_proc, freq > 0.1)
imzfile <- tempfile(fileext=".imzML")
writeMSIData(mse_proc, file=imzfile)
mse_re <- readMSIData(imzfile)

workflows.name: unsupervised_spatial_analysis_and_segmentation
workflows.intent: Perform unsupervised dimension reduction, feature colocalization, and spatial clustering/segmentation on an unlabeled MSI dataset.
workflows.stages:
1. Run Principal Components Analysis (PCA) using PCA()
2. Run Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF) using NMF()
3. Find colocalized features using colocalized()
4. Perform spatial shrunken centroids clustering using spatialShrunkenCentroids()
5. Extract top features for clusters using topFeatures()
6. Perform spatial Dirichlet Gaussian mixture modeling (spatial-DGMM) using spatialDGMM()
workflows.code:
pca <- PCA(mse, ncomp=3)
image(pca, type="x", superpose=FALSE, layout=c(1,3), scale=TRUE)
plot(pca, type="rotation", superpose=FALSE, layout=c(1,3), linewidth=2)
plot(pca, type="x", groups=mse$design, linewidth=2)
nmf <- NMF(mse, ncomp=3)
image(nmf, type="x", superpose=FALSE, layout=c(1,3), scale=TRUE)
plot(nmf, type="activation", superpose=FALSE, layout=c(1,3), linewidth=2)
plot(nmf, type="x", groups=mse$design, linewidth=2)
coloc <- colocalized(mse, mz=1003.3)
ssc <- spatialShrunkenCentroids(mse, r=1, k=3, s=c(0,6,12,18))
image(ssc, i=1:3, type="probability", layout=c(1,3))
plot(ssc, i=1:3, type="statistic", layout=c(1,3), linewidth=2, annPeaks="circle")
ssc_top <- topFeatures(ssc[[2L]])
dgmm <- spatialDGMM(mse, r=1, k=3, weights="gaussian")
image(dgmm, i=c(5, 13, 21), layout=c(1,3))
plot(dgmm, i=c(5, 13, 21), layout=c(1,3), linewidth=2)
coloc2 <- colocalized(dgmm, mse$square)

workflows.name: supervised_pixel_classification
workflows.intent: Train and cross-validate classification models to predict pixel classes (e.g., disease vs. normal) based on mass spectra.
input: aligned_peaks.imzML (preprocessed MSI dataset with known pixel class labels)
workflows.stages:
1. Perform cross-validation for Projection to Latent Structures (PLS) using crossValidate()
2. Train a PLS model using PLS()
3. Visualize predicted response values using image()
4. Perform cross-validation for spatial shrunken centroids classification using crossValidate()
5. Train a spatial shrunken centroids classifier using spatialShrunkenCentroids()
6. Extract top predictive features using topFeatures()
workflows.code:
cv_pls <- crossValidate(PLS, x=mse2, y=mse2$class, ncomp=1:5, folds=run(mse2))
pls <- PLS(mse2, y=mse2$class, ncomp=4)
image(pls, type="response", layout=c(1,3), scale=TRUE)
plot(pls, type="coefficients", linewidth=2, annPeaks="circle")
plot(pls, type="scores", groups=mse2$class, linewidth=2)
cv_ssc <- crossValidate(spatialShrunkenCentroids, x=mse2, y=mse2$class, r=2, s=c(0,3,6,9,12,15,18), folds=run(mse2))
ssc2 <- spatialShrunkenCentroids(mse2, y=mse2$class, r=2, s=9)
image(ssc2, type="probability", layout=c(1,3), subset=mse2$circleA | mse2$circleB)
plot(ssc2, type="statistic", linewidth=2, annPeaks="circle")
ssc2_top <- topFeatures(ssc2)
subset(ssc2_top, class == "B")

workflows.name: differential_abundance_testing
workflows.intent: Perform statistical hypothesis testing to identify mass features that are differentially abundant between experimental conditions.
input: aligned_peaks.imzML (preprocessed MSI dataset with experimental design metadata)
workflows.stages:
1. Perform sample-based means testing using meansTest()
2. Rank and filter differentially abundant features using topFeatures()
3. Perform segment-based means testing by first segmenting samples independently with spatialDGMM()
4. Fit linear models on the segmented data using meansTest()
5. Rank and filter segment-based test results using topFeatures()
workflows.code:
mtest <- meansTest(mse3, ~ condition, samples=run(mse3))
plot(mtest, i=1:10, layout=c(2,5), ylab="Intensity", fill=TRUE)
mtest_top <- topFeatures(mtest)
subset(mtest_top, fdr < 0.05)
dgmm2 <- spatialDGMM(mse3, r=2, k=2, groups=run(mse3))
stest <- meansTest(dgmm2, ~ condition)
plot(stest, i=1:10, layout=c(2,5), ylab="Intensity", fill=TRUE)
stest_top <- topFeatures(stest)
subset(stest_top, fdr < 0.05)
